einzeiler: A satirical interview with Poseidon reveals why the god of the sea is so deeply unlikable.
kurzfassung: The host interviews Poseidon in a framed comedy bit, examining the sea god's underwhelming role in major myths. Despite controlling oceans and earthquakes, Poseidon emerges as petty, insecure, and obsessed with petty grudges. The episode also explores the Philippine folklore creature known as the Alan.
stichpunkte: Poseidon is interviewed about his life and stories in a satirical podcast format.
Unlike Zeus, Poseidon frequently takes out his insecurities on vulnerable mortals like Medusa.
He claims his domain covers the entire foundation of the earth, making him responsible for earthquakes.
His pursuit of Amphitrite involved sending sea creatures across the land and using a dolphin as a wingman.
Poseidon's involvement in the Trojan War and various monster disputes highlights his retaliatory nature.
He consistently lost territorial contests to fellow Olympians like Athena, fueling his deep resentment.
The creature segment covers the Alan, a Philippine monster that rewards polite travelers and punishes child-boilers.

clips.hook: Why Poseidon preferred the ocean over the sky or the underworld
clips.text: The sea god dismisses his brothers' domains as boring and praises his own territory for the constant stream of travelers and worshippers.

clips.hook: The fatal commute of Poseidon's underwater search party
clips.text: Countless aquatic creatures combed the dry land for the fleeing Amphitrite, perishing within minutes from suffocation.

clips.hook: Calling out redundant terminology in ancient monster names
clips.text: The host points out that using the phrase Cetus sea monster repeats the exact same word twice, prompting an annoyed defense.

clips.hook: The staggering number of children fathered by the sea god
clips.text: Production notes reveal dozens of documented offspring alongside bizarre shapeshifting encounters involving rams and golden fleece.

clips.hook: A drastic parenting test involving a boiling cauldron
clips.text: A desperate traveler tries an extreme method to prove a monster infant had been fed while escaping with stolen meat.

beschreibung:
🔱It's Poseidon's turn.
On the podcast. Not to be king of the gods. He's actually totally not mad that his little brother is king. Because Zeus isn't the king of him. But Poseidon does do everything his brother says. Not because Zeus told him to, though. He just planned to do it anyway, so no problem.
😈 The Creature: The Alan

Just don't boil Alan's kids and you're good.
